title: Active Wear
oneLiner: An installation of twenty shirts that explores digital activism and the emotions behind it.

cover.alt: A white shirt with the word DEMOCRATIC hangs in the background; in front, a phone screen shows the AR layer with yellow text panels, held up by a visitor.

facts.Context: Bachelor's project, supervised by Prof. Erich Schöls
facts.Tools: Unity (C#, AR Foundation, ARKit), screen printing, graphic design

sections.label: Aim
text: Active Wear is an installative examination of digital activism and the emotionality behind it. The aim is to give access to activist practices and to encourage participation.

media.alt: White shirts with black screen prints hang from the ceiling on thin cords in a dark room; words such as SOCIAL and COURAGE are printed on them.

sections.label: Twenty shirts
text: For activist actions to succeed, many different people have to come together. Here they are represented by twenty second-hand shirts, each with its own screen print and a title for an aspect of activism that matters for democracy. The prints derive from activist or physical photographs and carry a short text on the inside. As in social movements, some shirts are passive and analogue, others proactively call for interaction: scanned with a smartphone they open augmented-reality experiences that question, provoke or invite action.

media.alt: A white T-shirt held by clips in front of a grey wall, printed with the word DECISIONS and a fine line drawing.
A hand turns a sleeve inside out and reveals a short printed text on the inside of the shirt.
Two visitors seen from behind; one holds up a phone and scans a hanging shirt.
Four phone screens of the AR layer: a golden sphere on a shirt, a yellow panel with a date and place of a protest, large yellow lettering, and a counter above a glowing button.

sections.label: Two layers
text: The shirts are deliberately monochrome, while the digital layer uses the strong colors of activist visual language. One typeface connects both. The title plays with "activewear", sportswear turned into a vehicle for civic engagement.

media.alt: Detail of a screen print: the word COURAGE in white on a black bar, surrounded by outlined figures holding signs.
A hand holds a screen-printing frame with a red edge against a white wall.
